summary: Make khao soi a small tasting project: try two bowls at different shops, then compare broth richness, spice, noodle texture and the effect of lime, pickled greens, shallots and chilli oil. A Chiang Mai local guide describes Khun Yai as a lighter, fragrant version and Mae Sai as thicker and spicier, but recipes vary and no single shop defines the dish.
whyGo: A side-by-side tasting makes the soft egg noodles, crisp topping and sour, fresh garnishes easier to notice.
Two contrasting neighbourhood shops turn a quick meal into a flexible half-day food outing.
You can form your own preference without treating a ranking or authenticity claim as settled fact.
bestFor: Curious eaters who enjoy curry, noodles and comparing small flavor differences
Independent travelers happy to use a map and order at casual lunch shops
People with enough appetite to split bowls or return on a second day
skipIf: You dislike coconut-rich curry or cannot eat wheat and egg noodles
You need a guaranteed vegetarian, halal or allergy-safe meal without confirming ingredients directly
You want a long, leisurely meal or cannot manage queues and informal seating
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes per shop including a possible queue. For two full bowls, spread the comparison across two days or share smaller tastes; these are planning estimates.
cost: Plan roughly THB 55–120 per bowl, based on a Chiang Mai guide's 2026 visits and citywide range; prices vary by meat, portion and venue and should be checked on site. Two bowls plus local rides and drinks could total about THB 250–500 per person (planning estimate). Carry cash.
hours: Khao Soi Mae Sai: Michelin lists Monday–Saturday 08:00–16:00, Sunday closed. Khao Soi Khun Yai: Thailand's tourism authority lists 10:00–14:00, Sunday closed. Both are daytime shops; arrive before lunch rush and allow for sell-outs. December holiday hours are unconfirmed.
bestTime: Go mid-morning on a weekday, before the lunch peak. Because Khun Yai's listed service window is short, check its current status before building the comparison around it.
gettingThere: The shops are in different areas: Khun Yai is by the north side of the Old City near Chang Phueak Gate; Mae Sai is at 29/1 Ratchaphuek Road in Chang Phueak/Santitham. Use a ride-hail car or red songthaew and show the exact pin; walking between them is not a useful plan. Transport fares and journey times vary with traffic, so budget separately and treat any app quote as current-day guidance.
booking: Plan for walk-in service; no confirmed reservation requirement was found. Michelin says Mae Sai manages its own bookings and advises contacting the restaurant, while the tourism listing gives Khun Yai's phone as +66 90 651 7088. Call ahead for current opening, larger groups or dietary questions.
accessibility: Step-free entry, accessible toilets, wheelchair clearance and queue seating were not confirmed for either shop. The casual, busy format may be difficult for some visitors; contact the venue directly if access needs affect your choice.
practicalTips: Order the same meat at both places if you want to compare broth and noodles; chicken is a common first choice, though today's menu can differ.
Taste each broth before adding anything, then add lime, pickled mustard greens, shallots and chilli oil a little at a time.
Record your own notes on richness, heat, noodle bite and garnish balance. Descriptions such as 'lighter' or 'spicier' are guide impressions, not fixed recipes.
Ask about stock, curry paste, fish sauce, shrimp and shared cooking for dietary needs; a vegetable topping does not guarantee a meat-free broth.
Carry small cash and keep a flexible alternative in case a shop is closed or has sold out.
decemberNotes: This is an everyday food outing, not a seasonal event. No December 2026 holiday schedule was published in the sources checked; verify Christmas and New Year opening close to the visit. December is busy in Chiang Mai, so allow extra ride time and avoid relying on a single short service window.
uncertainties: Current itemized menu prices are not posted in the official listings; cited bowl prices come from a local guide's visits earlier in 2026 and can change.
The tourism authority's Khun Yai schedule and Michelin's Mae Sai schedule may change, and neither guarantees food availability until closing.
Dietary accommodation, accessibility features, reservation availability and December holiday hours were not established.
Shop-specific flavor descriptions are guide observations; individual batches and personal tastes differ.
